Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin! The English openers- Rory Burns and Dominic Sibley make their way out in the middle. Tim Southee will open the proceedings with the ball.

New Zealand have decided to declare with their lead being 272. Meaning that England need 273 to win this Test. It will be interesting to see how they approach the last couple of sessions. The key for New Zealand is to take early wickets and get into the inexperienced English middle order.
.. Day 5, Session 2 ...

Right then! New Zealand have extended their lead in the first session and would look to do so further after Lunch. Unfortunately, the rain has brought the first session to an early end but let us hope that overs are not lost due to this. Will we get a result in this game? Or will it end in a draw? We will find out. Do join us in 40 minutes for the second session of Day 5. And pray that the rain doesn't play spoilsport!

The English bowlers had a fairly decent session with the ball. They bowled in the right channels and were getting the ball to get past the edge on quite a few occasions. Ollie Robinson continued to impress on his debut as he picked up the early wicket of Wagner. Broad too got his first wicket in the form of Latham and Wood dismissed Taylor. But the luck didn't favour them on a few occasions as even some of the edges were going to the ropes. Even their skipper Root got a wicket as Nicholls decided to take him on. Post Lunch, the priority of the bowlers will be to restrict New Zealand's lead.

New Zealand came out with intent to bat today and that intent was to score runs at a brisk pace. Wagner went back in the hut after hitting a few boundaries early in the session. But then came the stand between Latham and Taylor. They notched up runs at a brisk pace with Taylor being the aggressor. But unfortunately for New Zealand, both of them fell in quick succession. They did lose wickets in quick succession but the good thing for them was that whichever batsman was coming in, scored a few brisk runs before getting out. Post Lunch, Colin de Grandhomme and BJ Watling will look to score quick runs and with Colin de Grandhomme looking in ODI mode, it should make for some entertaining batting.

It was drizzling for a while but it has gotten heavier now. The umpires have decided to take an early Lunch. That brings an entertaining first session to an end. The lead for New Zealand is now 272 and it will be interesting to see how the approach the innings post Lunch.

Hello and welcome to the final day of the first Test between England and New Zealand at Lord's. The game is interestingly poised with New Zealand currently in lead. But if they have to win this game, they need to give their bowlers a scoreboard cushion and more importantly give them enough time to knock the English batters out. For England, their first priority will be to knock the New Zealanders out soon. Who will come out on top of today? Will we get a result? Or will this Test end in a draw? We will find out. Stay tuned for more updates!

Right! That is all we have from Day 4. It seems very unlikely that we will have a result in this game, but both teams will still try to force the same on the final day of the Test. The action on Day 5 will begin at 1100 local (1000 GMT). We hope to have your company for the same. Until then, goodbye and take care!

If not for the resistance shown by the centurion, Rory Burns, and some good batting displays from the debutant, Ollie Robinson and also James Anderson towards the end, as Jimmy helped Burns get to his ton, England would not have finished on a total of 275, but sadly for them, they were still behind by more than 100 runs. It was a tough start to their bowling as both Anderson and Broad tried to get that elusive breakthrough, but it just seemed to evade the veterans. It was then Robinson who struck twice and ended the day on a slightly better note for the hosts.

New Zealand started the day in top, top fashion as they went through the middle order and pushed the hosts on the back foot. Southee got his name engraved on the Lord's Honours Board, as he ended with 6 wickets to his name. Jamieson finished with 3, while Wagner got the solitary wicket. They let the last wicket stand between Burns and Anderson go on for longer than they would have wanted, but it was an overall good bowling display. With the bat, the duo of Latham and Conway played slow but steadily to ensure that they do not lose a lot of wickets on Day 4, but Conway and then, Williamson were Robinson's targets. After that, Latham and nightwatchman, Wagner survived until stumps.

Another great day of Test cricket between England and New Zealand. The third day of the Test was washed out and we have been lucky that there have been no interruptions on Day 4. Both the teams have fought tooth and nail and at the end of the day, it all seems even-stevens, with both teams having a say in the day.

NOT OUT! England takes another review. Good length delivery on off, coming back in, Conway looks to drive but misses his shot. The ball carries through to James Bracey who holds onto the catch. England thinks they have heard something and Joe Root goes for the review. Ultra edge confirms there was no bat involved. England loses their review. Conway survives.
Another review! This is for caught behind too. Nothing on Ultra Edge and so, will be not out. Review lost for England!

NOT OUT! Comes over the wicket, Pitches it outside off, seaming away from the batsman. Latham looks to defend off the front foot but misses. The ball hits his back pad and carries through to the keeper. England appeal but the umpire isn't interested. They take a review at the last moment for caught behind, but Ultra edge confirms there is no bat involved. Now, they will check for LBW, as the Ball Tracker shows that the ball is clipping the stumps but it's an umpire call. The onfield decision stays.

Review time! With a second to go on the timer, Root takes the review, for this caught behind appeal. Looks like it hit the backpad, and not the bat and hence, won't be caught behind. Now, they check for LBW and the impact is deemed to be umpire's call and so, it won't be LBW too. The review is retained though.
